summary: Anthropic states that the US government issued an export control directive forcing it to suspend all customer access to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models over an alleged jailbreak-related national security concern, which Anthropic is complying with while disputing the underlying finding.

mechanisms.reason: A government export control directive forces suspension of access to two named frontier models for all foreign nationals, a direct national-security-based access restriction on model access.
mechanisms.quote: The US government, citing national security authorities, has issued an export control directive to suspend all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 by any foreign national, whether inside or outside the United States, including foreign national Anthropic employees.

mechanisms.reason: Two commercially deployed models are being abruptly disabled for all customers, directly reducing served inference volume for those models.
mechanisms.quote: The net effect of this order is that we must abruptly disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all our customers to ensure compliance.

practices.reason: Any team building on Fable 5 or Mythos 5 must immediately migrate off these models with no advance notice, an unplanned but mandatory integration change.
practices.quote: we must abruptly disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all our customers to ensure compliance

practices.reason: The post describes extensive red-teaming and defense-in-depth jailbreak-resistance methodology, informative for how a lab evaluates safeguard robustness but largely internal and not directly transferable.
practices.quote: Anthropic worked with the US government, the UK AISI, multiple private third-party organizations and internal teams to red-team Fable’s safeguards for thousands of hours in total.

notable_reason: A US government directive forcing a frontier lab to abruptly disable two flagship deployed models over a national-security jailbreak concern is an unprecedented regulatory intervention worth immediate attention.
